newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares poised for further rise - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares poised for further rise - analysts.

text.p: Slovenian shares looked poised for further growth, analysts said on Monday, citing strong foreign interest, expectations of good results, and the nomination of a new prime minister as reasons for the optimism.
"Shares could continue to gain for several months although technical downward corrections are possible," Karmen Korbun, a trader at Austrian bank Creditanstalt, told Reuters.
Since January 6, the SBI share index has risen 12.8 percent to reach 1,303.98 points on Monday.

"The growth started as soon as it became obvious that Drnovsek had good chances of forming the government. The rise is based on foreign buying, which accounts for some 50 percent of turnover," said Nina Jarc at bank Nova Ljubljanska Banka.
Last Thursday parliament gave centre-left Liberal Democrat leader Janez Drnovsek the mandate to form a new government.
Drnovsek, whose party won most of the votes in an inconclusive November 10 general election, returned to power with the slimmest of margins by 46 parliamentary votes to 44.
"Investors are satisfied that Drnovsek got another mandate to form the government as that means stability although he may have a hard time forming the government," Korbun added.
She said she thought the good business results of some major listed companies were also pushing prices up.
"Foreign investors think current share prices are reasonably based on the profitability of major companies, for instance Lek, and share prices of similar companies in other markets," Korbun said.
"Prices are also up due to small offers as most small shareholders of newly privatised companies regard the investment in shares as a long-term one," Jarc said.
She said investors were most interested in drug company Lek, food company Kolinska, bank SKB, health resort operator Terme Catez, trading company Mercator and chemical producer Helios.
But analysts said the growth could be limited if foreigners decided to cash in their profits.

"When prices go up so fast, downward corrections usually follow. Therefore I expect shares will track sideways in the second half of January with the index remaining at the current level," said Toni Apollonio, an analyst of bank A banka.
